kill_fact: The net-debt bridge that converts enterprise value into per-share value in every one of the record's three cases is wrong by roughly $1.06bn because it counts only ONE of the two borrowing lines on the balance sheet. The record states net debt of $485m as 'borrowings of $981m less $495m of cash at 30 June 2026'. The $981m is the SHORT-TERM debt line alone. AMETEK's Q2 2026 balance sheet, filed with the 4 August 2026 release, also carries long-term debt of $1,055,541 thousand, plus finance-lease obligations of $274,770 thousand (current $61,826k + non-current $212,944k). On the record's own stated ex-lease definition net debt at 30 June 2026 is $980,633k + $1,055,541k - $495,446k = $1,540.7m, not $485m; including finance leases it is $1,815.5m. That is 3.2x the figure subtracted. The bear thesis itself SURVIVES this - it is the bear's own arithmetic that was too generous, and correcting it lowers every level by ~$6-7 per share and makes the risk/reward worse, not better. So this is a repricing, not a thesis kill: bear $168 -> $162, base $255 -> $250, bull $300 -> $295. It also reverses a claim the record makes elsewhere: the record declared the scan's net-debt-to-earnings figure of 0.72x 'stale' and 'roughly three times too high'; on the filed balance sheet actual net debt of $1.82bn against ~$2.5bn trailing EBITDA is ~0.73x, so the scan was right and the analyst was wrong. AMETEK is not a 0.2x-levered business.
corrections: (1) MATERIAL - net debt at 30 June 2026 is $1,540.7m ex-lease (or $1,815.5m including finance leases), not $485m. The record dropped the $1,055.5m long-term debt line. Carried through to all three levels on the record's own segment-EBITDA schedule and its own 229.845m diluted share count (which IS correct - filed Q2 2026 weighted-average diluted shares are 229,845 thousand): bear EV $38.8bn -> $162.1/sh; base EV $59.0bn -> $250.0/sh; bull EV $67.7bn + $1.6bn acquisition overlay = $69.3bn -> $294.8/sh. (2) MATERIAL CONSEQUENCE - at the live price of $255.15 on 11 August 2026 the stock now trades ABOVE the corrected base fair value of $250.0. The record's expected_return_pct of +3.37% (computed off $246.69 vs $255) becomes approximately -2.0%. The bear's central claim - 'the base case sits barely above the current price... the asymmetry currently points the wrong way' - is not merely intact but has crossed over: there is now no positive expected return to the base case at all. (3) MATERIAL - the bear's analyst-positioning evidence is stale. The bear asserts 'the freshest analyst target on file - Morgan Stanley at $245.00, dated 10 July 2026 - is below where the stock trades today' and 'the whole street range is $230 to $303'. Six houses refreshed post-print on 5-6 August 2026 (Truist, Citigroup, KeyBanc, RBC, DA Davidson, BNP Paribas). Current consensus price target is $273.00, median $272.50, range $230 to $316. Coverage did NOT stay stale through the print; the freshest targets are above the price, not below. This cuts AGAINST the bear's 'the market has finished looking' framing and is corrected here for the file. (4) MINOR - the record's non-bear-side claim that trailing free-cash margin and gross-margin expansion verify does hold: TTM to 30 June 2026 gross profit $2,876.7m on revenue $7,863.9m = 36.58%, and Q2 2026 revenue of $2,044,397k is +15.0% on $1,778,056k a year earlier. No compression finding; the GM-trajectory attack fails. (5) MINOR - the 4 August 2026 press release does NOT disclose the $4.11bn backlog figure or the 1.12 book-to-bill ratio; those are call/IR-deck figures, not press-release-verifiable. Orders growth of 28% IS in the release verbatim. The bear's adverse assumption (backlog plateauing at $4.1bn) is therefore built on a number I could not confirm from the wire release, though it does not move the arithmetic.
